title: A hand-written slot grammar with grammatical edits and reuse matches the entropy and the near-copies, but not the singletons or the page reuse, and the gap widens with size
statement: One independently specified procedure, frozen before measuring and fitted on no folio. Token formation: prefix + core + suffix, each drawn from a hand-written EVA-like inventory (20 prefixes, 23 cores, 21 suffixes, extended with simple two-part compositions to 60, 86 and 53) under fixed Zipf weights of exponent 1.2; no glyph-transition table is learned. Local reuse: with probability 0.25 a word is one of the last 15 words with one slot redrawn, kept only if the result is exactly one glyph from the source (a grammatical one-glyph edit); with probability 0.2 it is a whole copy of a word from 300 to 15 words back. Measured by pouring its words into the manuscript's certain paragraph-token slots (seed 1, after a 500-word burn-in) at three budgets. 2,000 tokens (training-page layout): manuscript H2 1.97, singletons 0.744, one-glyph copies of the last ten words 0.229, longer words already on the page 0.191, types 894; procedure 2.015, 0.663, 0.224, 0.093, 976. 5,461 tokens (evaluation layout): manuscript 1.940, 0.711, 0.210, 0.311, 1,907; procedure 2.079, 0.615, 0.238, 0.202, 2,123. 15,000 tokens (training layout): manuscript 1.959, 0.693, 0.219, 0.286, 3,740; procedure 2.111, 0.558, 0.243, 0.164, 4,406. Development runs on the evaluation layout: the bare grammar without reuse gives H2 1.986 but singletons 0.584 and near-copies 0.127; random one-glyph edits instead of grammatical ones push H2 to 2.3 to 2.5; smaller inventories bring H2 to 1.96 and near-copies to 0.26 but singletons down to 0.49; flatter weights bring singletons to 0.70 but H2 to 2.41. Answer for this family: a token grammar and a local reuse rule can match conditional entropy and the rate of near-copies without learning the manuscript's transition table, but not together with its singleton-rich vocabulary and its within-page reuse; the manuscript has fewer word types than the procedure yet more of them occur once, meaning a heavily reused core of familiar words and a long tail of one-off forms, and its singleton share falls more slowly with size (0.744 to 0.693) than the procedure's (0.663 to 0.558). The procedure on the record that meets all of these, R-017, learns a glyph chain from the public pages. Settings were chosen on the practice split.
check: Rebuild the grammar and reuse rule from this description, pour into the manuscript's token slots at 2,000, 5,461 and 15,000 tokens, and compare glyph_cond_entropy 2, hapax_share, near_copy (10, 4), page_reuse (4) and type counts.
